chunks: And with the former chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (blessings of God be upon him), used to say to the people of Kufa: 'O people of Kufa, do you think that I do not know what would mend your ways?! Indeed I do, but I hate to reform you by corrupting myself.'

key_terms.فساد نفسي: Corrupting myself — compromising one's moral integrity and principles for the sake of political expediency
key_terms.يصلحكم: What would mend/reform your situation — in the political context of Kufa, refers to bringing order and loyalty

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about reforming people without corrupting oneself?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Imam Ali (AS), during his caliphate in Kufa (35-40 AH), would admonish the Kufans with this powerful statement. As the political capital of his government, Kufa was rife with internal dissent, tribal rivalries, and wavering loyalties. Imam Ali refused to employ corrupt tactics — bribery, deception, or compromising principles — to bring order, even though he knew exactly what would work. This reflects his unwavering commitment to moral integrity in governance, preferring difficulty with justice over ease with corruption.
